races.note: A special election for the rest of the term: Representative Joseph A. Stagni resigned effective June 30, 2026, and the Speaker of the House's proclamation of June 30 set the special primary for November 3 and the special general election for December 12. It is an open primary: every candidate of every party is on one ballot; more than half the votes wins the seat, otherwise the top two meet on December 12. Louisiana elects its whole Legislature in odd years (next in 2027), so no other legislative seat is on the 2026 ballot.

la-sos-2026-local-races-in-a-parish.title: Candidate Inquiry, Races in a Parish: the November 3, 2026 lists of all 64 parishes
la-sos-2026-local-races-in-a-parish.note: Each parish's list was read twice, as the portal's CSV export and as its page (election id 344), and the two had to agree office by office and name by name. From the export, by column name: Election, Parish, OfficeTitle, OfficeTitleDescription, NumberToBeElected, BallotFirstName, BallotLastName, BallotSuffix, Party, Outcome; from the page: the office title, the number to be elected, the first line of the name and party columns and the status cell. The export's other columns (Address, City, State, Zip, Address Mismatch, Phone, Email Address, Race, Gender, Filed Date) are never read, nor is the rest of each candidate's block on the page, and only the kept cells are saved. 5,083 candidate rows: 677 federal (left to the federal pages), 152 for the state offices this loader's state part reads, and 4,254 local, of which 4,254 are placed: 4,013 candidacies in 2,377 contests, each in exactly one (a contest on several parishes' lists has a row in each: 120 contests). Status words: Unopposed (1,658 candidates in 1,515 contests, declared elected and not on the ballot); Withdrew, Other/Disq and Deceased (102, left off). 37 offices have no candidate left on the list (the page shows them; the export has no row for them). The list gives no ballot position: the law arranges each office's candidates alphabetically by surname (R.S. 18:551(C)), the list and the results site's race files are in the same order, and that order is kept as the ballot order of the contested offices. Louisiana has no write-ins. The sha256 here is of the answers' own hashes joined.

local_calendar.t: November 3, 2026 is Louisiana's open primary for the local offices filled in congressional election years: district judges and district attorneys, parish, family, juvenile and city court judges and city marshals, school boards in every parish but Orleans and Lafayette, justices of the peace and constables, the Plaquemines Parish president and council, and the mayors, police chiefs and councils of the municipalities on the fall cycle. Every candidate is on one ballot with the party printed; a majority elects, any seat left goes to the general election on December 12, and a candidate nobody opposed is declared elected and left off the ballot. Sheriffs, police juries and the other parish offices elected with the Governor (next in 2027), the Orleans and Lafayette school boards, and the municipalities that vote in the spring or in 2028 are not regularly on this ballot, so a seat of theirs here is a special election.
local_calendar.s: La. R.S. 18:402 and 18:511 (Louisiana State Legislature); Louisiana Secretary of State, Schedule of 2026 Elections and Offices Regularly Scheduled for Congressional and/or Presidential Elections

Left off: 102 candidates marked withdrawn, disqualified or deceased. Not loaded: the 100 constitutional amendments and local propositions, the December 12 general election, and who holds each office today.
